symbols.note: Returns family key for cross-language filter; None stays None.

claims.why: The scope check is in _mint_from_diffs, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: CROSS-FILE ONLY: must_include never contains a symbol defined in the file chosen as target.
claims.why: This filtering logic is in _mint_from_diffs, not in this chunk.

claims.text: _mint_from_diffs re-checks non-emptiness once, after filtering, and mints nothing (with a reason) if nothing survives.
claims.why: The function _mint_from_diffs is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: JUNK: a diffed name that fails _is_junk_label never becomes a must_include entry -- dropped names land in labels_filtered_junk (sorted).
claims.why: The junk filtering logic is in _mint_from_diffs, not in this chunk.

claims.text: CROSS-LANGUAGE: a label may only come from a file whose language FAMILY (_language_family(languages.spec_for(...).name)) matches the TARGET's.
claims.why: Cross-language filtering is in _mint_from_diffs, not in this chunk.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule is run against every anchor CANDIDATE's current content before target selection.
claims.why: Floor rule application is in _mint_from_diffs, not in this chunk.

claims.text: _IDENTIFIER_RE: unicode-aware, allows leading/embedded $, on top of the universal letter/digit/underscore identifier shape.
claims.why: Regex r'^(?:[^\W\d]|\$)[\w$]*$' matches: starts with letter (\w without digits) or $, then word chars or $. Unicode-aware because \w matches Unicode letters/digits in Python 3.

claims.text: Keyword check: deliberately NARROW, and case-SENSITIVE.
claims.why: _JUNK_KEYWORDS contains only lowercase keywords; _is_junk_label does not lowercase name. See line 145: 'return name in _JUNK_KEYWORDS'.

claims.text: _is_junk_label: Checked name-shape-first (a non-identifier like <anonymous> never reaches the keyword set at all).
claims.why: Function first checks _IDENTIFIER_RE.match(name); if False, returns True immediately. Only if True does it check keyword set.

claims.text: _language_family: None (no LanguageSpec) stays None and therefore never equals any real family, same fail-closed behavior as before.
claims.why: If lang_name is None, returns None immediately. Then any comparison with real family strings will be False.

claims.text: _git: stdout on success, None on ANY failure (missing git, not a repo, bad ref, timeout, non-zero exit). Minting must degrade to 'nothing minted', never raise.
claims.why: Catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError; returns None if proc.returncode != 0. No other exceptions escape because subprocess.run with timeout only raises those.

claims.text: _is_linked_worktree: Detection is the git on-disk contract, not a path heuristic: git worktree add writes .git as a FILE holding a gitdir: pointer, whereas a primary checkout has .git as a DIRECTORY.
claims.why: Line 210: checks dot_git.is_file() – returns False if .git is a directory. Line 213: reads file and checks for 'gitdir:' prefix.

claims.text: A SUBMODULE also has .git as a gitdir: file, and a submodule checkout is perfectly permanent -- refusing to mint from one would be a false refusal.
claims.why: The function continues after reading the pointer to inspect the admin directory structurally; the chunk ends before that structural check is complete. Cannot verify claim.

claims.text: The admin directory the pointer resolves to is inspected STRUCTURALLY: commondir and gitdir together appear only in the linked-worktree admin layout. Requiring BOTH means an unreadable or unexpected target fails toward 'not ephemeral', i.e. toward minting.
claims.why: The structural inspection code is not fully present in this chunk; it ends at line 227. Cannot verify.
